newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates mixed in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates mixed in quiet session.

text.p: Interbank rates were mixed in quiet Kuala Lumpur trading with continual inflow of funds absorbed by steady market demand, dealers said.
"Funds are coming back in the system but they are well absorbed," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Some three billion ringgit of funds which had flowed out this month for local festivals were expected to return to the market from last week.
Dealers said one-week interbank rate was quoted at 6.80/7.00 percent from 6.80/90 on Monday.
Two-week money was at 7.20/25 from 7.00 and three-week at 7.20/30 against 7.00/20.
One-month rate was at 7.20/25 percent from 7.23/25 previously. The three-month rate was at 7.30/35 percent from 7.30 and six-month to one-year were unchanged at 7.30/35.
Dealers said they expect the interbank rates to remain on the soft side in the immediate term as funds remained ample.
"On the whole, the rates are easy," said a dealer at another bank.

The release of Malaysia's 1996 trade balance data was welcomed by market players as it showed a narrowing deficit. The data came on the back of positive figures on the current account balance and gross domestic product (GDP) growth reported over the weekend.
But dealers and economists said the central bank was unlikely to ease interest rates any time soon as the economy remains robust.

Said Desmond Supple, chief economist (Asia Pacific) at BZW: "This is a very pleasant surprise and confirmed the sharp improvement in Malaysia's economic fundamentals we have seen in the past 12 months.
"The current account (deficit of 11.0 billion ringgit in 1996) fell below 5.0 percent of GDP in 1996 from 8.8 percent in 1995."
